mechanism_narrative: The four-week rise in WORKPLACES (-26.9 to -17.7) reflects a steady reopening of office-based employment, which generates incidental retail and dining trips on commute routes, pushing RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved monotonically from -26.9 to -17.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trajectory, indicating the commute-linked retail spillover does not hold.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 5.0 (a drop of at least 1.1 points from current levels), it signals households are spending markedly less time at home, which translates into a short-term surge in discretionary retail and recreation visits within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 10.1 to 6.1 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks after RESIDENTIAL crosses below 5.0, falsifying the home-time-to-retail substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: A joint recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility compounds to amplify RETAIL_REC growth beyond what either series would predict alone, because transit-enabled commuting restores both access to retail corridors and disposable time for shopping.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -56.9 to -49.7 while WORKPLACES rose from -28.6 to -17.7 over the same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth rate over the next four weeks is no greater than what a single-series (WORKPLACES-only) model predicts, indicating no synergistic interaction between TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, simultaneous recovery of PARKS and TRANSIT mobility indicates relaxed public restrictions, which within two weeks extends to permit greater retail and recreation activity as businesses resume normal operating capacity.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS recovered from -19.9 to -14.0 and TRANSIT from -56.9 to -49.7 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next two weeks despite continued joint recovery in PARKS and TRANSIT, rejecting the policy-relaxation linkage.

mechanism_narrative: The volatile week-to-week swings in PARKS (e.g., -8.1 to -19.9 to -14.0) reflect short-horizon weather or seasonal variability rather than structural change, and such noise does not propagate into RETAIL_REC within a single week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS shows non-monotonic swings of over 10 points across consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC exhibits strong co-movement (same-direction change exceeding 3 points) with PARKS swings within the same week, indicating the seasonal noise is not isolated from retail behavior.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained near baseline (0.6 to 1.1) for four consecutive weeks, indicating essential-goods demand is saturated and stable; this stability implies no additional behavioral shock is suppressing or inflating RETAIL_REC in the coming week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays within +/-1 point of baseline for the prior four weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM ranged only from 0.6 to 1.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC moves by more than 3 points in either direction within one week despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining stable, indicating essential-goods stability is not predictive of retail trend direction.

mechanism_narrative: Under an active reopening regime, the combined rebound of WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and decline in RESIDENTIAL together signal a coordinated policy-driven return to pre-pandemic routines, which compounds to drive a stronger four-week increase in RETAIL_REC than any single series would suggest.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL falls week-on-week, for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:All three series moved consistently (WORKPLACES up, TRANSIT up, RESIDENTIAL down) over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to accelerate beyond its prior four-week trend despite the three-series co-movement persisting, rejecting the compounded reopening-signal hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: If the week-on-week rate of improvement in WORKPLACES mobility decelerates (e.g., the gain shrinks to less than half of the prior week's gain), it signals the reopening momentum is plateauing, which will stall further gains in RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week improvement falls below 50% of the prior week's improvement
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES gained 9.7 points from t-1w to t-0w after gaining 9.7 from t-2w to t-1w, suggesting a plateau risk
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next two weeks even after WORKPLACES improvement decelerates by more than half, rejecting the momentum-deceleration linkage.
